answer_text: Sodium hydroxide reacts with sulphuric acid as 2NaOH + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O. The base is neutralised to a salt and water. It is also a double displacement reaction because Na+ and H+ exchange partners. It is not a precipitation reaction, since sodium sulphate dissolves in water. Phenolphthalein is pink in the alkaline NaOH and turns colourless once enough acid has been added to destroy the basic medium.
